analyst_view.overall: Early view: Elversberg have scored four against both Gladbach and Mainz and add set-piece goals from Felix Keidel and Maurice Krattenmacher, so they are dangerous at home. Stuttgart are in the Champions League and had a long injury list in early November, including Angelo Stiller, though several were expected back after the break.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. I lean slightly higher: Elversberg's games have produced 35 goals in nine and Stuttgart's 30, with Stuttgart conceding three at home to Gladbach and two at Leverkusen. Both sides attack more than they defend.

corners.text: The site expects 11.5 corners, 6.8 for Stuttgart. That Stuttgart share is high for an away side, and Elversberg have been willing to attack at home rather than sit deep, so I lean lower.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards. Elversberg had one player booked at Dortmund and Stuttgart's card count has depended on the opponent, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The site has 32.9 shots, which is high. Stuttgart's 18.7 away looks generous for a side that may rotate around Champions League football, so I lean slightly lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 on target. Two sides with efficient finishing (Elversberg's set pieces, Stuttgart's Ermedin Demirović and Jamie Leweling) keep this close to the number despite my lower shot view.
